decisions.quote:
Here, we address the critique first by conducting a replication
       study using an independent sample of 9,300 subjects. This study replicates the gene-environment inter-
       action of the 5HTT gene variant with church attendance, but not the association with MAOA. We then
       focus on the general argument of the critique, showing that many of its characterizations of the literature
       in genetics and in political science are misleading or incorrect.
decisions.reason: The source positively reports new observations retesting the earlier published finding. The shipped and blind record types both correctly say replication. Removing this particular mismatched or alternate-report row is a separate original-identity decision and does not change the empirical type of its current paper. The earlier type decision incorrectly used not_a_replication to express row removal. The retained valid pair is row 207 (Fowler and Dawes, 2008). No outcome is transferred to the removed original. Independent primary abstract, Introduction and explicit new-sample account verify this distinction; all earlier decisions are preserved.

decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files do not yet exist for da46803ed980caec. Fowler and Dawes (2013) conducts a single empirical replication—of Fowler and Dawes (2008, Two Genes Predict Voter Turnout, Journal of Politics 70(3): 579-594, DOI 10.1017/s0022381608080638)—using newly genotyped Wave IV Add Health subjects, which is already paired and resolved in shipped row 207 (paired_target_index 0). Shipped row 478 lists Stein and Vonnahme (2008, Engaging the Unengaged Voter: Vote Centers and Voter Turnout, DOI 10.1017/s0022381608080456) with the exact same 5HTT/MAOA outcome quote as row 207. Stein and Vonnahme (2008) does not appear anywhere in the text or reference list of Fowler and Dawes (2013), and no second original paper is empirically re-tested. Therefore, row 478 is a spurious duplicate row with a mismatched DOI/citation and must be removed.
